title: Making a game has become a game
author: TheOldAgeDeveloper
selftext:
A game runs on feedback loops, fast gratification, a little grinding, and a reward at the end. AI turned creating games into that same loop.

AI has made making games easier, but you still have to grind a little. And that’s a good thing. The grind is what makes it fun, and the reward feels better when you earned it.

The community is also improving fast in this space. People are sharing mechanics as simple building blocks that AI can snap together, so making a game is starting to feel like playing with Lego.

Here’s what I think about where this is going, and why you should go build your dream game, even if it sucks.

I explain that a little better in my video: [https://youtu.be/wBGMeZh1izI](https://youtu.be/wBGMeZh1izI)

comments.author: DeanRayGames
comments.body: Making a game has sort of become a "game" in the sense that you make progress, you get rewarded with more of your creation coming to life. But that's for the first 90% of the creation process. The last 10%, the balance, the bug fixing, the optimization, the playtesting for the 100th time... that's NOT fun... but it's what separates a prototype/beta from a complete game. And it's a slog. Most people probably give up and move onto the next project when it stops being "fun" to make progress. But overall I agree with you!

replies.author: Xieboid
replies.body: Agreed. Designing and building prototypes is fun. Actually finishing and shipping a game is work.

replies.author: Wrathicus
replies.body:
This is dead on lol. I built my own card scanning tool for my shop and it was super neat at first! "I don't have to pay for things that don't give me the tools I need anymore?!" Vibing fun quickly turned into mapping out all the little shit that's broken, or was built without the correct prompt context which seems easy but feels so tedious 😅 

It'll all be worth it in the end though, don't give up at the finish line people!

replies.author: DeanRayGames
replies.body: Absolutely. And there's nothing wrong with "taking a break" from a project that you're feeling a little burn out on, but you MUST define ahead of time how long your "break" is going to be so it doesn't turn into an indefinite hiatus and then eventually a background thought that pops into your mind from time to time and then into something you don't even think about at all!

comments.author: batmessiah
comments.body: This is my view of it as well.  I've dropped $300 on different AI tools to develop my games, and it's totally worth it, because I'm having more fun developing these games than I ever have playing other people's games.  It's weird, but it's an insanely cool outlet for ideas and creativity.

replies.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
replies.body: Same here. I'm running 2 Claude subscriptions plus a few other subscriptions as well to build my game. I'm having just as much fun, if not more fun, building it than playing a game. This is something I've wanted to build for years though, so that probably plays a part

replies.author: TheUniverseOrNothing
replies.body:
Yea it’s hilarious when people say I’m wasting money. I’ve got hammered and spent more in one night that I don’t remember.

This is investment into my mental health if it doesn’t turn profitable. I’m so happy spending time building my dream game.
